title: Simultaneous selected counter increments
statement: Let $l$ be a natural number, let $x$ be a bit word, let $p$ be an input-head position, and let $a$ select a subset of the $l$ coordinates. For each coordinate $i$, let $n(i)$ be a natural-number counter value, and suppose one common width bound $W$ satisfies that the binary representation of every $n(i)$ has length at most $W$. Starting with one counter on each tape, each in its selection-dependent starting control with head at cell $0$ and tape holding the binary representation of $n(i)$, the bank machine after $2W+2$ steps has every component in its return control with head at cell $0$; tape $i$ holds the binary representation of $n(i)+1$ when $a(i)$ is true and of $n(i)$ otherwise. The input position remains $p$ and the output remains empty.
hypotheses_covered: For every coordinate $i$, the binary representation of $n(i)$ has length at most $W$
replaced: For every input word, input position, selection vector, counter values, and common width bound $W$ covering all the values' binary representations, running the counter bank for $2W + 2$ steps increments exactly the selected coordinates, leaves the unselected ones unchanged, and restores every head to zero; the cost is independent of the number of counters.
